title: Combinatorics and the classical definition of probability

steps.title: Where probability began
steps.idea: Probability theory grew out of questions about games of chance, in the 1654 letters between Pascal and Fermat.

steps.title: The urn scheme
steps.idea: Choosing k balls out of n can be ordered or not, with or without replacement. Each of the four cases has its own count.
formula: ordered, without replacement:  Aₙᵏ = n! / (n − k)!
unordered, without replacement: Cₙᵏ = n! / (k! (n − k)!)
unordered, with replacement:   C(n + k − 1, k)
Cₙᵏ are the coefficients of Newton’s binomial (a + b)ⁿ
steps.example: n = 3, k = 2: 9 ordered pairs with replacement, 6 without, 3 unordered without, 6 unordered with.

steps.title: Classical probability
steps.idea: When all elementary outcomes are equally likely, the probability of an event is the share of outcomes that favour it.

steps.title: Statistical definition
steps.idea: Repeat the experiment many times: the relative frequency of the event settles near its probability.
steps.example: Buffon tossed a coin 4040 times and got 2048 heads (W = 0.5069). Pearson tossed it 24 000 times and got 12 012 heads (W = 0.5005).

steps.title: Bertrand paradox
steps.idea: "A random chord" has no single meaning. Three natural sampling schemes give three different probabilities that the chord is longer than the side of the inscribed triangle.

steps.title: Pairwise is not mutual independence
steps.idea: Three events can be independent in pairs and still depend on each other as a triple.
formula: P(AB) = P(A)P(B), P(AC) = P(A)P(C), P(BC) = P(B)P(C)
